newsitem.title: USA: Continental Air settles commission suit.
newsitem.headline: Continental Air settles commission suit.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc. said Tuesday it had agreed to pay about $5 million to settle an antitrust suit claiming that major carriers had conspired to fix commissions paid to U.S. travel agents.
A hearing will be held Thursday on the case, which continues against Delta Airlines, American Airlines, NW, United Airlines and USAir, a spokesman for the American Society of Travel Agents said.
Trans World Air Lines settled the case out of court in May 1995, he said.

The suit was filed by the American Society of Travel Agents and 20 travel agents. Continental denied all claims in the suit, but said it was settling to avoid the risks and expenses of further litigation.
The society of travel agents said the proceeds from the settlement would be distributed to travel agents.

The suit, filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota, claims that seven major U.S. airlines conspired to fix and maintain the commissions paid to U.S. travel agents for domestic travel.
The class action combines 14 separate lawsuits that were filed beginning February 1995, soon after the airlines imposed commission caps.
Previously, travel agents received a commission of 10 percent of the price of a ticket for U.S. travel.
Following the change, the carriers paid a fixed $25 commission for a domestic roundtrip ticket worth $250 to $500, and $50 for a ticket worth $500 or more.
The settlement, which will be subject to a hearing and court approval, provides for the complete release of all claims and dismissal of the case against Continental.
Continental's class A stock rose 25 cents to $22.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
